hints: Notice the system starts at rest, so total momentum is zero. Use $m_1v_1 = m_2v_2$ with $2 \text{ kg}$ at $2 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to find the speed of the $1 \text{ kg}$ trolley.
The stored elastic potential energy is converted into kinetic energy of both trolleys. Recall $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$ must be calculated separately for each mass.
Calculate $\frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 2^2$ and $\frac{1}{2} \times 1 \times v^2$ for the 1 kg trolley, then add them to find the initial stored energy.
walkthrough: Initial total momentum is zero because the trolleys are held together at rest on the horizontal surface.
Apply conservation of linear momentum after release. Let $v$ be the speed of the 1 kg trolley to the right: $2 \times 2 = 1 \times v$, so $v = 4 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Assume no work is lost. The stored elastic potential energy equals the sum of the final kinetic energies: $E = \frac{1}{2}m_1v_1^2 + \frac{1}{2}m_2v_2^2$.
Substitute values with units: $E = \frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times (2)^2 + \frac{1}{2} \times 1 \times (4)^2 = 4 \text{ J} + 8 \text{ J}$.
Add to get $E = 12 \text{ J}$ with correct energy unit. This is option D.

options.A: This is only $\frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 2^2 = 4 \text{ J}$, the kinetic energy of the 2 kg trolley. It ignores the kinetic energy given to the 1 kg trolley.
options.B: This is the result if both trolleys are assumed to move at $2 \text{ m s}^{-1}$. Momentum conservation requires the lighter 1 kg trolley to move faster than the 2 kg trolley.
options.C: This is only $\frac{1}{2} \times 1 \times 4^2 = 8 \text{ J}$, the kinetic energy of the 1 kg trolley. The stored energy must supply kinetic energy to both trolleys.
options.D: Total kinetic energy is $4 \text{ J} + 8 \text{ J} = 12 \text{ J}$, which must have come from the elastic potential energy of the spring.
